summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted for recurrent left knee prosthetic joint infection, presenting with increased pain, swelling, drainage, and leg swelling. She underwent two surgical washouts with spacer exchange and synovectomy, during which she experienced significant blood loss requiring seven units of packed red blood cells. A catheter-associated Pseudomonas UTI was identified, prompting a switch from cefazolin to cefepime for two weeks before transitioning back to cefazolin. Her anemia, related to both acute blood loss and chronic kidney disease, was managed with transfusions. Diarrhea persisted but was mild and non-C. diff, likely antibiotic-related. A small non-occlusive clot near the PICC line was monitored without intervention. She was stabilized on warfarin for DVT prophylaxis, had her pain controlled with MS Contin and Dilaudid, and was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics, wound care, and follow-up with orthopedics, infectious disease, and nephrology.
